newsitem.title: USA: Peru's Fujimori hopes rebels will give some ground.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori hopes rebels will give some ground.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said on Sunday he was optimistic about starting formal talks with Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages in Lima, hoping the guerrillas might give ground on their key demand.
The rebels have demanded freedom for their jailed comrades and have refused to hold talks with the government unless that issue is discussed.

While Fujimori did not say the rebels would alter their demand, which has been rejected by the government, he told the CNN International television network he hoped they would not directly refer to it in a forthcoming statement.
"In the coming document of the MRTA (Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement) we may read it is not written expressly the liberation of MRTA prisoners," Fujimori said in English.

All recent statements by the MRTA have expressly called for talks to include their demand for the release of about 400 jailed comrades in return for their 72 hostages. Fujimori said in Toronto on Saturday he planned to resume talks, which have been on hold for weeks because the government refuses to discuss the rebels' main demand.
Fujimori added the government had been holding informal talks with the rebels through the visits of Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani to the besieged Japanese ambassador's home.
"We have advanced, in fact, for beginning this preliminary dialogue. We have advanced in such a way that some bases have already been established," Fujimori said.
He added he expected further progress to be made on the statement "in the next days."
"So we should be a little optimistic that this problem may have a resolution," he said.
Fujimori flew to Washington on Saturday after an emergency summit in Toronto with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on the crisis.
At Saturday's summit, Fujimori and Hashimoto agreed to push for direct talks with the rebels, even though they reiterated they would not consider the demand for the freedom of MRTA rebels in prison.

The MRTA rebel leading the operation in Lima, Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, appeared Saturday to dash any hopes of a quick settlement, reiterating that he would release his captives only after all his jailed comrades were freed.
"We have come for one goal and we will not renounce it," Cerpa said from inside the residence in a walkie-talkie interview with the CBS Telenoticias network.
Before returning to Lima Monday, Fujimori is scheduled to meet with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and other State Department officials to discuss the standoff with the MRTA.
The rebels originally took more than 500 hostages Dec. 17 during a lavish cocktail party at the diplomatic mansion but have freed most of them.
The remaining 72 captives in the mined and booby-trapped residence include two Peruvian ministers, the Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors, about two dozen Japanese businessmen and Fujimori's brother.
